After breakfast, join a full-day group excursion to Machu Picchu with an English-speaking guide.

Machu Picchu is known as the ‘Lost City of the Incas’, hidden among mountains and jungle. Its buildings were constructed from large stone blocks fitted together without mortar.

The Spanish did not find the city after the fall of the Inca Empire. It became widely known after the American archaeologist Hiram Bingham’s expedition in 1911.

Lunch follows the tour. Then return to Cusco by train, where you will be met and transferred to your hotel.
View of the terraces at Machu Picchu and the surrounding mountain peaks, Peru
Machu Picchu: green terraces and stone ruins against a mountain backdrop

After breakfast, set out on an excursion to the Sacred Valley.

Its fertile land and mild climate made the area important to the Incas. Ruins of towns, temples and agricultural complexes survive here.

The itinerary includes Urubamba, associated with the country residence of the Inca ruler Huayna Capac, the archaeological complex of Pisac, the ceremonial centre at Ollantaytambo, Chinchero and the amphitheatre-shaped terraces of Moray.

Near Pisac, you can visit a market selling silverware, ceramics and leather goods.

Another stop is the Awanakancha centre, where you can see llamas, alpacas and vicuñas, learn how they are cared for and see how their wool is dyed.

Lunch is a buffet at Inka House, a restaurant serving Peruvian cuisine.

After the excursion, transfer back to the hotel.

This full day in the Sacred Valley takes in several kinds of Inca sites. Pisac sits on a hillside and is linked to a large archaeological complex, Ollantaytambo preserves ceremonial buildings, Chinchero has Inca walls alongside a colonial church, and Moray is distinguished by its circular agricultural terraces. The separate stop at Awanakancha focuses on Andean animals and how their wool is processed.
